gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long the built-in-cable chargers keep up full power. Smartzone.de measured the UGREEN Nexode 100W Retractable dropping from 100 W to 65 W after an average of 35 minutes. Andreas Gohr (splitbrain.org) measured the UGREEN X605 holding a steady 55 W into a laptop for about an hour at a 56 °C peak. Techtest.org ran the Anker Nano 35W Retractable (A2658) at a constant 35 W for several hours and measured 0.16 W idle draw.
standout_why: I read whoahome.com's compact-charger roundup (2026-10-10) in full. It covers six chargers, none with a built-in cable, and says outright that it lists no measurements, only maker figures checked October 10, 2026. I could not read three other result pages. Both Tom's Hardware pages came back with only the headline, and curl to them was refused. The Guardian could not be fetched, and Android Authority returned HTTP 403. So I can't confirm that none of them covers a retractable-cable charger. None of the result titles mentions retractable or built-in cables, and ChatGPT's answers showed corded-block bundles (Anker 33W, Belkin 40W, onn 20W, Anker 67W) plus, in one chat, the Anker Nano 35W block with a retractable cable, with no measured data on any of them. Measured sustained output for the retractable models our page lists is very likely new against these results, but because three rivals were unreadable I rate it 2, not 3.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN Nexode 65W Retractable (X605) as the main pick and changes how the 100W should be presented. The 100W's laptop advantage lasts about 35 minutes before it throttles to 65 W (Smartzone), and its built-in cable is not where the extra power goes away. Gohr found the X605 steady at 55 W for an hour, while the Mcdodo FreeGo (about 54 W to 41 W) and Baseus Enercore (58 W to 47 W) in the same test fell back. For phones, the Anker A2658 held its full 35 W for hours (techtest.org). Its 0.16 W idle draw makes it fine to leave plugged in. No reviewer measured the Belkin 67W or the ESR 45W, so neither can be shown on measured data.

findings.label: Sustained power into a laptop over about 1 hour (Andreas Gohr, splitbrain.org)
findings.value: 55 W, steady from start to the 1-hour mark
findings.source_title: Retractable Cable USB-C Chargers (splitbrain.org, Andreas Gohr)
findings.note: Gohr read power from the laptop's charge controller ADC (ISL9241) every 5 s with ectool. The CPU was held at 100% with stress, and the battery was drained to about 40% first. The URL dates the post July 2026, and the page has no other date.

findings.label: Peak surface temperature after about 1 hour of laptop charging (Gohr)
findings.source_title: Retractable Cable USB-C Chargers (splitbrain.org, Andreas Gohr)
findings.note: Highest infrared thermometer reading. In the same test: Mcdodo FreeGo about 53 °C, Topadre 65W 64 °C, Baseus Enercore 47 °C, unbranded YKEJCLD 69 °C.

findings.label: Built-in cable length, measured (Gohr; ChargerLAB)
findings.value: 67 cm including the connector (Gohr); about 68 cm (ChargerLAB)
findings.source_title: Teardown of UGREEN Nexode 65W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X605), ChargerLAB, 2025-08-06
findings.note: UGREEN rates the cable at 70 cm (2.3 ft). ChargerLAB measured 197 g. Its POWER-Z KM003C reading shows the cable tops out at 20 V 3 A (60 W) and the USB-C port at 20 V 3.25 A (65 W).

findings.label: Efficiency range and heat under a 4-hour 65 W load (Michael Barton, techtest.org)
findings.value: Efficiency 79% to 90%. Close to 90 degrees under a continuous 65 W load at 27–30 °C room temperature. Measured weight 201 g.
findings.source_title: UGREEN X605 Test: 65W Ladegerät mit ausziehbarem USB-C Kabel im Test (techtest.org, 2025-07-04)
findings.note: The load ran for more than 4 hours over the USB-C port on what the author called the hottest day of 2025. The text says 'fast bis zu 90 Grad' (nearly 90 degrees) without saying where on the charger it was measured. The per-load efficiency chart is an image, so only the 79–90% range could be taken from the text. Mains voltage is not stated.

findings.label: Sustained 100 W output under a constant electronic load (Jan, smartzone.de)
findings.value: Throttles from 100 W to 65 W after an average of 35 min. At that point: 57 °C on the housing, 73 °C at the ports.
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 100W Ladegerät mit einziehbarem Kabel im Test (smartzone.de, 2025-08-21)
findings.note: Load was an electronic load at a preset constant current. Ambient temperature is not given. Smartzone also measured efficiency of 79% at 10 W, 84% at 20 W, 87% at 30 W and 45 W, and 89% at 65 W and 100 W (86% average), plus a weight of 304 g. With USB-C2 and USB-A in use together, each drops to 7.5 W.

findings.label: Measured cable length and weight (ChargerLAB)
findings.value: Cable about 72.5 cm. Weight about 303.8 g. Body 57.02 × 50.53 × 69.08 mm.
findings.source_title: Teardown of the UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (ChargerLAB)
findings.note: The page as fetched showed the date November 4, 2026. ChargerLAB's KM003C reading shows the cable at 20 V 5 A and PPS 5–21 V 5 A. The thermal protector trips at 65 °C, and no operating temperatures were measured.

findings.label: Sustained output, efficiency and idle draw (Michael Barton, techtest.org)
findings.value: Held 35 W constantly for several hours. Efficiency 81.1% at very low load to 89.5% at full load. Idle draw about 0.16 W. Measured weight 117 g. Each port gets at most 17.4 W when both are in use.
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charger A2658 mit 35W und InstaCord-Kabel im Test (techtest.org, 2025-07-27)
findings.note: The 100% load ran for 'einige Stunden' (several hours). No °C reading was given; the author wrote only that it did not get especially warm. Mains voltage and ambient temperature are not stated. The article does not say whether the 17.4 W two-port figure is per port or combined.

unsourced: Belkin UltraCharge Retractable 67W (WCH022): no reviewer- or lab-measured output, temperature or efficiency. I searched for ChargerLAB, Notebookcheck and general USB-meter or sustained-output reviews, and found only Belkin's own internal charge-time claims (iPhone 17 Pro Max 0–50% in 23 min) and B&H's spec listing.

ESR Xtend 45W Retractable (2D001): no reviewer-measured figures. I searched for ChargerLAB, lygte-info and general tests, and found only ESR's own claim of staying below 77 °C at 25 °C ambient, plus lygte-info data for a different ESR 45W car charger, which does not apply.
Temperature in °C for the Anker A2658: techtest.org gives none, and I found no thermal-camera test.
Per-load efficiency for the UGREEN X605: techtest.org's chart is an image, and the text gives only the 79–90% range.

Measurements of ChatGPT's picks (Anker 33W 2-port with 6 ft cable, Belkin 40W dual, onn 20W, Anker 67W 3-port): I did not reach Android Authority (HTTP 403), Tom's Hardware (only the headline came back) or The Guardian (fetch refused), so I could not tell whether those rivals publish measured figures.
